topics.label: Introduction to cancer causes and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture, introduces its speaker and objectives, and is not yet part of the substantive material.

topics.label: Cancer as clonal evolution in a permissive microenvironment
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains cancer as the evolution of mutated cell clones that depend on a supportive microenvironment.

topics.label: Interacting influences on cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics frame cancer risk as an outcome of interacting influences rather than either pure chance or a single exposure.

topics.label: Geographic variation as evidence of cancer risk factors
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic uses differences in cancer incidence across regions and migrant populations to consider environmental and inherited contributions to risk.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can contribute to cancer and illustrate this with the development of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Carcinogenic mechanisms and context-dependent effects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how exposures can damage DNA or promote tumour growth, and how their effects depend on biological context.

topics.label: Methods for assessing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe ways to identify carcinogenic exposures and evaluate their effects, while noting the limits of each approach.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion: cancer risks and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This closing subtopic recaps the lecture’s conclusions and frames exposure decisions in terms of risks and benefits.
